samples.summary: Task doc contradicts the shipped behavior: checklist claims a fixpoint loop, code implements a bounded 8-pass loop that refuses instead
samples.evidence: Checklist item `- [x] stripConfigDirectives() loops until the source stops changing` and Approach line "strip config carriers to a **fixpoint** rather than one pass". The implementation (`mermaid.ts:317-325`) runs at most `MAX_STRIP_PASSES = 8` passes and returns `null` (a refusal) if the source is still changing. The design doc was updated to say "bounded, not a fixpoint", but the task plan it derives from was left stale, so the two records of the same decision disagree.

samples.summary: Refusal rules are broad enough to reject legitimate diagrams, and the whole-block refusal is a coarse remedy for the narrow layout-window problem
samples.evidence: `IMAGE_METADATA_RE = /@\s*\{[\s\S]*?["']?img["']?\s*:/i` scans across the entire fence body, so any `@{ … }` metadata block anywhere followed by the text `img:` anywhere later (e.g. a prose label "img: see attachment") refuses the diagram; `FETCH_TAG_RE` matches `<\s*\/?\s*(?:…|svg|math|input|object|source|…)`, so a prose label such as `A["x < input field"]` or `A["a < svg thing"]` is refused. The chosen remedy (refuse the whole fence, show source + message) removes documented mermaid capabilities (image shapes, HTML label styling) rather than neutralising just the fetch; the file itself notes a CSP is the better answer. Flagged as approach/scope fit — the false-positive mechanics are for the correctness lens.

samples.summary: Two near-duplicate CSS fetch regexes and a tag list duplicating FORBID_TAGS knowledge, in one module
samples.evidence: `CSS_SOURCE_FETCH_RE` (line 364) is a hand-narrowed copy of `CSS_EXTERNAL_RE` (line 454) — same alternation minus `image(`/`src(` — and `FETCH_TAG_RE` (line 338) re-encodes the fetch-carrier tag knowledge already expressed in `FORBID_TAGS` (line 429) with a different, larger list. Three overlapping sources of truth for "what fetches" will drift; a single shared list/derivation would keep them in step.

samples.summary: Refusal set covers `img:` shape metadata but not other network-capable metadata (e.g. architecture/`icon:` icon packs), leaving the stated boundary uneven
samples.evidence: `prepareFenceSource()` enumerates exactly three carriers (fetch-capable tags, `img:` metadata, CSS url). Nothing in the module or the design doc addresses `icon:` metadata / architecture-diagram icon resolution, which mermaid resolves through registered icon packs (network-capable in the general case). If that path can fetch during layout, the stated invariant ("refuses a fence whose SOURCE carries a fetch") is not met; if it cannot, the design doc should say so, since it already enumerates architecture icons as an unguarded `foreignObject` path.

verdict.reason: The cited code genuinely exists (mermaid.ts:338-404, 229-236, 272, 635) and the todo's "Deliberately not done" section was indeed not extended, so the factual claim is partly accurate — but it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (1) No stated Non-Goal is exceeded: docs/design/notes/notes.md:49-63 lists the notes Non-Goals and none covers fence-source refusals; the todo's "Deliberately not done" (todo.md:54-61) is about not collapsing DOMPurify to the SVG-only profile, a different subject. (2) No acceptance criterion is failed — the added refusals serve the issue's own outcome (close the beacon vector), as the paired lessons doc records: htmlLabels:false closes only the label path while imageSquare()/`A@{img:…}` and the unguarded-foreignObject diagram types still fetch in the live layout host (lessons.md:40-52), and the fixpoint loop needed a length+pass bound because maxTextSize is enforced inside render() (lessons.md:54-61). (3) Design-doc discipline is met in the canonical subsystem doc, not a parallel file: docs/design/notes/notes.md:464-497 documents the dompurifyConfig/flowchart/class pinning, the maxTextSize cap and the bounded strip, and notes.md:548-561 is a dedicated "Why the source is refused, not just sanitized" bullet naming the raw-tag rule, `img:` shape metadata and CSS url()/@import. (4) Neither CONTRIBUTING.md:59-65 nor docs/tasks/README.md requires the todo's plan prose to be kept exhaustive; leaving it behind the implemented scope is doc hygiene, i.e. minor, which never blocks. The finding cites no criterion, Non-Goal, duplicated module, or missing/parallel doc — the major thresholds for this lens.

searchedFor: Grep 'mermaid' across repo for other render call sites
finding.summary: Fix may only close the beacon for htmlLabels-guarded (flowchart-style) labels; the repo's own notes say several diagram types emit `foreignObject` regardless of `htmlLabels`, and nothing here addresses or covers those
finding.evidence: `renderPass()` sets `htmlLabels: false` and the tests exercise a flowchart fence. But PURIFY_CONFIG's new comment (mermaid.ts:259-264) and docs/design/notes/notes.md:525-527 both state that "venn text nodes, architecture icons, kanban, sequence" append a `foreignObject` with NO `htmlLabels` guard. Those subtrees are also parsed into the live `document.body` during the layout window that the issue identifies as the fetch boundary, so if any of them can carry note-supplied markup (an `` or inline `style` with `background:url(...)`), the issue's outcome (no beacon fires from a note) is only partially met — and the change adds no mitigation, follow-up, or test for those diagram types. Could not verify against the installed engine: `mermaid` is not present in node_modules in this tree.

verdict.reason: The finding says the change adds no mitigation, doc, or test for the diagram types that emit foreignObject regardless of htmlLabels. All three exist. (1) Mitigation: prepareFenceSource() (mermaid.ts:384-404) refuses the fence SOURCE before the engine runs, via label-path-agnostic rules: FETCH_TAG_RE (mermaid.ts:338-339) for fetch-capable raw tags (img/image/iframe/use), IMAGE_METADATA_RE (mermaid.ts:351) for img shape metadata, and hasCssFetch/CSS_SOURCE_FETCH_RE (mermaid.ts:364-373) for external CSS url() and @import. These are exactly the two attack shapes the finding hypothesizes (a raw img src, or an inline style with background:url). The module header states this rationale and names the unguarded-foreignObject types as its second bullet (mermaid.ts:69-93). (2) Doc: docs/design/notes/notes.md:548-565, bullet 'Why the source is refused, not just sanitized', says htmlLabels:false closes the label path and nothing else, and explicitly ties the raw-tag rule to those diagram types whose labels go through mermaid's own sanitizeText with a default allowlist permitting img src. The reviewer read notes.md:525-527 and stopped ~20 lines short of it. (3) Test on one of the named types: preview.test.ts:775-792 renders a sequenceDiagram fence carrying a raw img src and asserts engine.render was never called, with a comment naming venn/architecture/kanban/sequence; companion cases at :750-773 (img metadata) and :794-807 (CSS url) cover the other carriers, with a negative control at :809-819. The lessons doc section 'Closing one carrier of a class is not closing the class' (lessons.md:40-52) records this exact pushback and the source-refusal answer. The missing node_modules/mermaid is immaterial: the refusal is upstream of the engine and asserted by engine.render not being called, so it holds whichever label path a release uses.
